key_insight: Medical world models aim to go beyond static diagnosis by simulating how a patient’s state may evolve under different treatments.
clinical_relevance: This framework could help clinicians anticipate deterioration, compare intervention scenarios, and personalize care decisions over time.
method: Construct patient-state representations from longitudinal and multimodal health data.
Model clinical dynamics as an internal simulator of disease progression.
Use treatment-conditioned planning or reinforcement learning to support intervention choices.
evidence_signal: The paper is a review that synthesizes representative systems across foundation models, longitudinal modelling, disease simulation, treatment-effect estimation, reinforcement learning, and digital twins rather than reporting a single new benchmark.
watch_item: Plausible simulated trajectories may still fail to be clinically useful if they do not generalize well, remain interpretable, or reflect real-world treatment constraints.
paper_title: Medical world models: representing medical states, modelling clinical dynamics and guiding intervention policies
